title: $67,000 a Year Is How Much an Hour? (2026)
metaDescription: $67,000 a year is $32.21/hour at 40 hrs/week — $1,288.46 weekly, $5,583 monthly. Full 2026 breakdown with a federal take-home estimate.

hero.lede: Based on a 40-hour week worked 52 weeks a year (2,080 hours). Below: every pay-period equivalent, the rate at other workweeks, a 2026 federal take-home estimate, and how $67,000 compares with the U.S. median.

shortAnswer.heading: How much is $67,000 a year per hour?
shortAnswer.html: $67,000 a year is $32.21 an hour at 40 hours a week, 52 weeks a year (2,080 hours). That's $257.69 a day, $1,288.46 a week, $2,576.92 biweekly, and $5,583.33 a month — all gross. After estimated federal income tax and FICA, a single filer keeps about $55,965 a year, roughly $4,664 a month.

sections.title: What $67,000 looks like per paycheck.
sections.note: All figures are gross (pre-tax). See the take-home table below for the federal-only estimate after taxes.

sections.title: Where $67,000 stands in 2026.
paragraphs: Spread $67,000 across the 2,080 working hours in a standard year and you get $32.21 per hour. The same salary reads as $1,288.46 a week, $2,576.92 every two weeks, or $5,583.33 a month — all before a dollar of tax comes out.

By national standards it is a middle-of-the-pack wage — BLS data shows the median full-time worker earned $1,251 a week in Q2 2026, or roughly $65,052 a year, within a few percent of this salary. Household context matters too: as a single income supporting a family, $67,000 works harder than the same figure in a two-earner household, even though the per-hour arithmetic never changes.

sections.title: The hourly rate depends on your hours.
sections.note: Salaried roles rarely pay overtime — at 45 hours a week the same $67,000 effectively pays $28.63 per hour worked.

sections.title: From $67,000 gross to take-home.
sections.note: Single filer, standard deduction, no state/local income tax, no credits or pre-tax benefits. Your actual paycheck will differ.

sections.title: Why the 22% bracket doesn't mean 22% tax.
paragraphs: For a single filer in 2026, the $16,100 standard deduction trims $67,000 of wages down to $50,900 of taxable income. The last dollar is taxed at 22%, yet the average rate is far gentler: $5,910 of federal income tax works out to 8.8% effective, with another $5,126 going to FICA payroll taxes.

That leaves an estimated $55,965 a year of federal take-home — about $4,663.71 a month, or a total withholding rate of 16.5% before state tax. Run it through a 50/30/20 budget and the monthly split is roughly $2,332 for needs, $1,399 for wants, and $933 for saving or debt paydown.

faq.q: How much is $67,000 a year per hour?
faq.a: $67,000 a year is $32.21 an hour at 40 hours a week (2,080 hours a year). At 37.5 hours a week it rises to $34.36 an hour, and if you actually work 45-hour weeks it averages $28.63 per hour worked.

faq.q: How much is $67,000 a year biweekly?
faq.a: Gross biweekly pay on $67,000 is $2,576.92 ($67,000 ÷ 26 pay periods). After estimated federal income tax and FICA for a single filer, roughly $2,152.48 per check remains — before state taxes and benefits.

faq.q: How much is $67,000 a year after taxes?
faq.a: Using 2026 federal brackets and the $16,100 standard deduction, a single filer earning $67,000 pays about $5,910 in federal income tax and $5,126 in FICA, keeping roughly $55,965 a year ($4,663.71 a month). This is a federal-only estimate — state and local taxes reduce it further.

$67,000 is right around the U.S. median full-time salary of about $65,052 (BLS, Q2 2026: $1,251/week). Whether it is "good" depends heavily on your metro's cost of living, household size, and debt load — the same salary goes much further in a low-cost region than in an expensive coastal city.

faq.q: What tax bracket is $67,000 in for 2026?
faq.a: After the $16,100 standard deduction, $67,000 leaves $50,900 of taxable income, which puts a single filer in the 22% marginal bracket for 2026. Only income above each threshold is taxed at the higher rate, so the effective federal rate is just 8.8%.

methodology: Conversions are straight arithmetic on gross salary: $67,000 ÷ 2,080 hours (40 × 52) for hourly, ÷ 260 workdays for daily, ÷ 52, 26, 24 and 12 for the pay-period figures. No taxes are applied to those rows.

The take-home estimate uses 2026 federal brackets for a single filer with the $16,100 standard deduction, plus employee FICA (6.2% Social Security + 1.45% Medicare). It excludes state/local income tax, credits, and pre-tax benefits such as 401(k) or health premiums — so real paychecks will differ.
The median comparison uses BLS median usual weekly earnings for full-time wage and salary workers: $1,251/week (BLS, Q2 2026).
Educational estimates only — not tax, legal, or financial advice.
